_readme: Owner-controlled running order for the homepage business spotlight card. See SPOTLIGHT.md in the repo root for how to add a week. Every 'week' value is the WEDNESDAY the card flips, in America/Los_Angeles. The card is live from Wednesday 00:00 Pacific through Tuesday 23:59 Pacific, so it is already showing the new business before the Thursday social post goes out. If no row matches the current week the card renders nothing at all; the homepage is unchanged and nothing breaks.
_slug_rule: slug must be the live Around Town URL slug, exactly as it appears after /around-town/. Cross-check data/live-article-slugs.json. If the slug does not resolve on the live site, the card renders nothing.
_hold: Do NOT schedule air-and-fire-boulder-creek, wild-lilith-boulder-creek, good-vibes-boulder-creek or boulder-creek-golf-country-club until their corrections land (held 2026-09-09). Remove a slug from this list once its correction is published.

schedule.blurb: Their glass hangs in a Scotts Valley medical office, and the studio that made it is on Boulder Creek's main street. Two artists trained in Brooklyn and Venice, and an hour on the bench if you want to try it yourself.
When Highway 9 is a mess or the car is in the shop, the prescription still gets to you. The independent on Central Avenue delivers anywhere in the valley for free, and has been in town over 40 years.

Skye Herrick had owned his Boulder Creek house for two days when the CZU fire took him out of it. Gamers he'd never met mailed him models and paint. That's where the program his Pine Street shop runs today came from.

Dr. Kathie Gerrity took over in December 1985 and called it just a transfer of keys. One employee, an avocado-green telephone, and patient records on 4-by-6 index cards. Forty years on, the clinic is still here.

The rule at the door needs explaining: Springygirl doesn't take local donations or consignments. Spring Loftus buys her secondhand stock from nonprofits, so the money has already gone somewhere before a piece reaches the rack.

A special-education teacher picked up bar shifts at the Redwood Keg to help with his daughter's college costs. Customers kept telling him about the flume, old feuds and a drive-in nobody mentions anymore. Now those stories are on shirts.
He grew up around laundromats. She couldn't stand them. The building's been in his family since 1974, and in 2021 they pulled out the coin slots and put an app in their place.

In April 2020 the shop asked for $1,700 to get through the shutdown. Twenty-five people sent $1,875. Kim Brown has been grooming Boulder Creek's dogs since 1998, and it's the nervous ones people mention.
